articles.title: As razões de ex-marido para perdoar a ex-mulher acusada de matar seus 3 filhos: 'Teria me consumido por dentro para sempre' | G1
articles.standfirst: Em entrevista à rede americana CBS, o pai dos três menores afirmou também ter tido pensamentos suicidas.
articles.summary: Em entrevista à rede americana CBS, o pai dos três menores afirmou também ter tido pensamentos suicidas.
articles.body:
Patrick Clancy perdoou sua ex-esposa Lindsay Clancy, acometida de psicose pós-parto, pela morte dos três filhos do casal — Foto: Getty Images via BBC

Importante: esta reportagem contém detalhes sobre doenças mentais e discussões sobre suicídio que podem ser perturbadores para alguns leitores.

Patrick Clancy, ex-marido da mãe americana acusada de matar seus três filhos pequenos três anos atrás, declarou que teria ficado "consumido por dentro para sempre" se não a perdoasse pelo ocorrido.

Em entrevista à rede de TV CBS, parceira da BBC nos Estados Unidos, Clancy declarou ter feito todo o possível quando sua ex-esposa, Lindsay Clancy, lutava contra uma doença mental, nos meses anteriores ao estrangulamento dos menores.

Linday não negou tê-los matado, mas seus advogados defendem que ela não deve ser considerada legalmente responsável, já que sofria de uma doença mental grave.

No início deste mês, um juiz declarou a anulação do julgamento, pois o júri informou não ter conseguido atingir um veredito unânime sobre sua culpa ou não pelo assassinato.

A promotoria afirma que, no dia 24 de janeiro de 2023, Clancy estrangulou intencionalmente seus três filhos: Cora, de cinco anos; Dawson, de três; e Callan, de oito meses, na sua casa em Duxbury, no Estado americano de Massachusetts.

Clancy tem, agora, 36 anos. Ela ficou paralisada ao pular de uma janela do segundo andar e acompanhou o julgamento em cadeira de rodas.

Patrick Clancy testemunhou durante o processo sobre a deterioração da saúde mental da sua ex-esposa, depois de dar à luz.

A defesa argumentou que ela sofria de psicose pós-parto. Trata-se de uma condição pouco frequente, na qual as mulheres podem sofrer episódios de mania, depressão ou uma mistura de ambas, após o nascimento de uma criança.

"Eu não sabia como lidar com uma doença pós-parto", declarou o pai à CBS. "Acredito que as doenças mentais têm essa capacidade de serem tragicamente enganosas."

A defesa de Lindsay Clancy afirma que ela cometeu o crime enquanto era acometida de uma séria doença mental — Foto: Getty Images via BBC

O estado de saúde mental de Lindsay Clancy foi exatamente o que levou Patrick a perdoá-la.

"Vi manchetes dizendo, sabe, 'Mãe assassina', 'Assassina de bebês', 'Monstro'", afirmou ele. "E nenhuma delas era correta."

"Acredito que foi sua doença mental que provocou aquilo. Por isso, expressei estas palavras. E, em relação a perdoá-la, também senti que, se não chegasse a este ponto, eu me consumiria por dentro para sempre."

A reportagem da CBS questionou Clancy se ele sentia que havia falhado de alguma forma no período anterior a os assassinatos.

"Acredito ter feito o melhor que pude, com os recursos e o conhecimento que tinha naquele momento. Convivo com isso todos os dias", respondeu ele.

Nas semanas que se seguiram à tragédia, suportar o luto se tornou uma luta. Ele reconheceu ter sofrido pensamentos suicidas.

"Não pensei que chegaria a completar 35 anos", ele conta. "E estava totalmente em paz com esta ideia."

Ao longo das sete semanas de julgamento, Patrick Clancy foi alvo de uma intensa e hostil campanha na internet. Ele foi acusado de encobrimento e algumas pessoas afirmaram que ele teria algum grau de responsabilidade pelos assassinatos.

Transformado repentinamente em uma figura pública, os jornais publicaram fotografias suas viajando e ao lado da sua nova esposa, Rachel Danis.

Hoje com 36 anos, Clancy declarou que estas especulações eram "profundamente prejudiciais para o legado dos meus filhos".

"Sou uma enorme distração sobre o que realmente importa aqui, que é a saúde mental perinatal", afirma ele.

O pai destacou que, para ele, também havia sido pessoalmente "doloroso observar".

"E é difícil ficar em público. É possível que algumas pessoas, depois de observarem mentira após mentira após mentira, comecem a acreditar nelas e é com isso que acabamos ficando."

A intensa atenção da imprensa o levou a se mudar de Duxbury (uma cidade com 16 mil habitantes) para Nova York, para tentar recuperar o anonimato.

Patrick Clancy e sua nova esposa foram entrevistados pela CBS, emissora parceira da BBC nos Estados Unidos — Foto: Getty Images via BBC

Peter Clancy, agora, está formando família com Rachel Danis. Ele tem esperança de poder falar aos seus futuros filhos sobre seus irmãos.

"Acredito que todos os pais concordarão que temos relacionamentos diferentes com cada um dos filhos, mas todos são nossos filhos", ele conta. "E não vejo a hora de contar a eles sobre seus irmãos e sua irmã."

A anulação do julgamento deixa o caso sem solução e os promotores ainda não indicaram se irão pedir um novo processo.

A próxima audiência está marcada para o dia 29 de setembro, no Superior Tribunal de Plymouth, em Massachusetts.

Caso você seja ou conheça alguém que apresente sinais de alerta relacionados ao suicídio, ou tenha perdido uma pessoa querida para o suicídio, confira alguns locais para pedir ajuda:

O Centro de Valorização da Vida (CVV), por meio do telefone 188, oferece atendimento gratuito 24h por dia; há também a opção de conversa por chat, e-mail e busca por postos de atendimento em todo o Brasil;

Para jovens de 13 a 24 anos, a Unicef oferece também o chat Pode Falar;

Em casos de emergência, outra recomendação de especialistas é ligar para os Bombeiros (telefone 193) ou para a Polícia Militar (telefone 190);

Outra opção é ligar para o SAMU, pelo telefone 192;

Na rede pública local, é possível buscar ajuda também nos Centros de Atenção Psicossocial (CAPS), em Unidades Básicas de Saúde (UBS) e Unidades de Pronto Atendimento (UPA) 24h;

Confira também o Mapa da Saúde Mental, que ajuda a encontrar atendimento em saúde mental gratuito em todo o Brasil.

Para aqueles que perderam alguém para o suicídio, a Associação Brasileira dos Sobreviventes Enlutados por Suicídio (Abrases) oferece assistência e grupos de apoio.

articles.title: Hunter charged with manslaughter in shooting of woman he mistook for a deer: Police
articles.summary: The victim was identified by police as 39-year-old Santos Maria Chilel Soto.
articles.body:
A 74-year-old hunter has been arrested and charged in a homicide investigation in which police allege he fatally shot a woman in Delaware whom he allegedly mistook for a deer.

Walter Moorhead of Salisbury, Maryland, was charged with manslaughter and related crimes after allegedly shooting the woman while hunting Friday evening in a field near Ellendale, Delaware, according to the Delaware State Police.

"The preliminary investigation revealed that the victim was walking through the field with a man and two children while Moorhead was hunting deer from a ground blind. Moorhead believed he saw a deer and fired his rifle, striking the victim," the Delaware State Police said in a statement.

The victim was identified Sunday as 39-year-old Santos Maria Chilel Soto of Georgetown, Delaware, according to the state police.

The incident unfolded around 7:40 p.m. on Friday, according to the state police, who said troopers who were called to the scene provided lifesaving medical care to the victim, who was later pronounced dead at a hospital.

Troopers took Moorhead into custody after a preliminary investigation "determined that he had fired the shot that struck the victim," according to the state police.

In addition to the charge of felony manslaughter, Moorhead is facing three counts of first-degree reckless endangerment, as well as a count of possession of a firearm during the commission of a felony, state police said.

Moorhead was arraigned by the Justice of the Peace Court and released after posting a $43,000 cash bond, according to the state police.

Moorhead did not immediately return a call from ABC News on Sunday seeking comment at a phone number listed for him. It was unclear if he had hired an attorney.

The Delaware State Police said the shooting remains under investigation and asked anyone with information about the incident to call its homicide unit.

articles.title: Omagh bomb: Fourteen people linked to evidential activity, inquiry told
articles.summary: Twenty-nine people, including a woman pregnant with twins, died in the bombing in the County Tyrone town on 15 August 1998 - the biggest single atrocity in the Troubles.
articles.body:
Fourteen people have been linked to evidential activity in the days leading up to and on the day of the Omagh bombing, the inquiry into the explosion has heard.

Twenty-nine people, including a woman pregnant with twins, died in the bombing in the County Tyrone town on 15 August 1998 - the biggest single atrocity in the Troubles.

It came less than three months after the people of Northern Ireland had voted yes to the Good Friday Agreement.

The inquiry, which opened last year with 14 days of testimony from bereaved families and survivors, was established to determine if the bombing could have been prevented by UK state authorities.

Paul Greaney KC outlined the "working hypothesis" of the inquiry when it resumed its latest phase on Monday.

In 2009, a judge ruled that four men - Michael McKevitt, Liam Campbell, Colm Murphy and Seamus Daly were all liable for the Omagh bomb.

A fifth man, Seamus McKenna, was found not liable in the civil action and later died in a roofing accident in 2013.

In a statement to the inquiry, sitting at Bradford Court in Belfast, Greaney named McKenna, Daly and Murphy as among the 14 people linked to evidential activity.

Greaney told the inquiry: "The evidence suggests Colm Murphy sat like a spider in the centre of the web of the plan to detonate a bomb in Omagh."

Referring to the civil case, Greaney said that the fact that McKenna "was not found liable is not an outcome which binds this inquiry".

"Our working hypothesis is that, contrary to that finding, he played a key role," he said.

The use of telecommunications is a key part of the evidence in front of the inquiry and some of the most frequently referred to mobile phones have been assigned colours for ease of following their links.

The inquiry heard how it was "likely" that the Vauxhall Cavalier car used in the bombing was "stolen to order" in the days before the bombing.

Evidence was outlined that on 14 August 1998, the day before the bombing, a "test run" of the journey to the bomb site was carried out in a Volkswagen Golf car.

The inquiry heard about the time and locations of warning calls made ahead of the bomb exploding. Two calls were made to UTV, and one to the Samaritans.

The caller said a 500lb bomb had been left in Omagh and would explode in 15 or 30 minutes.

The call to the Samaritans said the bomb was in the centre of Omagh, 200 yards from the courthouse.

The warning calls were reported to the police within minutes. Royal Ulster Constabulary (RUC) officers were then deployed to the town.

The inquiry heard that the Army did not deploy to Omagh town centre before the detonation as the RUC did not ask it to.

Counsel for the inquiry set out the evidence that will be explored over the four weeks of the hearing.

It includes evidence from forensic scientists, DNA specialists, and handwriting experts.

Witnesses will include former PSNI chief constable Sir Ronnie Flanagan and Baroness Nuala O'Loan, former Police Ombudsman.

An Garda Siochana have also given evidence which will be shown to the inquiry as a pre-recorded video.

In closing the first day of chapter three of the inquiry, Paul Greaney KC said that the "devastating impact" of the Omagh bomb is at the heart of the inquiry.

"We know that there are very many people who have been waiting for those answers for nearly three decades. They have waited too long.

"They are entitled to those answers and we, the inquiry legal team, will play our part in delivering them."

The principal objective of this chapter of the inquiry is to understand how the bombing was carried out and by whom.

Among the witnesses this week will be a senior garda officer who is expected to provide initial evidence about the theft of the car used in the explosion.

It was stolen in Carrickmacross, County Monaghan, two days before the explosion.

The inquiry was established to determine if the bombing could have been prevented by UK state authorities.

The third phase is expected to last about four weeks.

The Omagh bomb exploded on 15 August 1998, killing 29 people including a woman pregnant with twins.

More than 200 people were injured in the blast.

No-one has ever been convicted of the atrocity.

Three days after the attack, the Real IRA released a statement claiming responsibility for the explosion.

It apologised to "civilian" victims and said its targets had been commercial.

No-one has been convicted of carrying out the murders by a criminal court.

In 2009, Michael McKevitt, Liam Campbell, Colm Murphy and Seamus Daly were all ordered to pay a total of £1.6m in damages to the relatives, but appeals against the ruling delayed the compensation process.

articles.title: Council ordered to pay £50k after blocking 81-year-old’s garden access; retired teacher says officials were ‘beyond childish’
articles.summary: UK News: Helene Ball, an 81-year-old retired teacher, has won a court battle against Derbyshire County Council after workers cemented a metal fence panel acros.
articles.body: Helene Ball, an 81-year-old retired teacher, has won a court battle against Derbyshire County Council after workers cemented a metal fence panel across a 3ft gap in the rear wall of her Matlock property in April 2023, blocking the gate that had provided access to her garden for years. Ball successfully proved the gate had been in use since the 1960s, establishing a right of way, and a first-tier tribunal ordered the council to pay £50,000 in costs. Here's how the dispute unfolded, and what Ball had to say about her three-year fight.How the council blocked Helene Ball's garden accessIn April 2023, Derbyshire County Council workers cemented a metal fence panel across a 3ft gap in the rear wall of Ball's Matlock property, blocking a gate she had relied on for garden access. While the wire fence itself was removed within a year, vehicle access to the street remained blocked throughout the entire legal process that followed, leaving Ball without full use of her property for years while the dispute worked its way through the system. The council has since created a new route for Ball through the site, which is currently up for sale as a small housing development.Helene Ball's fight to prove her right of wayBall took legal action against the council, successfully proving in her case that the gate at her address had been in continuous use since the 1960s. As a result of this evidence, a right of way was established, and a first-tier tribunal ordered Derbyshire County Council to pay £50,000 in costs. Speaking to The Telegraph after her legal victory, Ball said she had taught nine, 10- and 11-year-olds all her life but never expected a council to act so "babyish," describing its behaviour as "beyond childish" and "absolutely shocking."The council's conduct during the legal battleBall said the council did everything it could to bully her throughout the process, adding that after dealing with bullies at school as a teacher, she found herself being bullied again as a pensioner. She said the council tried to put her off pursuing the case, but that it had "messed with the wrong ones." Reflecting on the ordeal, Ball said the dispute brought her more than three years of stress, but that she and her supporters had ultimately proven the council had blocked her rights. In the tribunal ruling, Judge Robert Brown noted that some evidence presented by the council was "surprisingly combative."The political context behind the disputeThe fence's installation and the legal battle that followed began under the former Conservative administration at Derbyshire County Council. However, the case continued, and the ultimate tribunal hearing took place, under the council's subsequent Reform UK leadership, meaning the dispute spanned a change in political control at the authority before Ball finally secured her costs award and confirmed right of way.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.summary: US News: US President Donald Trump on Monday defended the move to ban top US media from White House calling it an \"assault on fake news\". This comes after MS N.
articles.body: US President Donald Trump on Monday defended the move to ban top US media from White House calling it an "assault on fake news". This comes after MS NOW, CNN and Politico said that they would sue the Trump administration to protect their First Amendment rights."The White House is not instituting an assault on the Free Press, something which I cherish. It is instituting an assault on the FAKE NEWS, something that has grown like Cancer in our beloved United States of America," Trump said in a post on Truth Social."It is corrupt, purposeful, pervasive, fully coordinated, and totally out of control. articles.title: North Carolina turned 3,000 tons of damaged concrete pipes and boxes into two artificial reefs, creating new habitat off the Outer Banks
articles.summary: US News: North Carolina has given two existing artificial reefs off the Outer Banks another 3,000 tons of material, using damaged and unusable concrete pipe an.
articles.body: North Carolina has given two existing artificial reefs off the Outer Banks another 3,000 tons of material, using damaged and unusable concrete pipe and boxes that would otherwise have required disposal. The N.C. Artificial Reef Program completed the two enhancement projects in May 2026, placing approximately 1,500 tons of recycled concrete at each site. The reefs, designated AR-230 and AR-250, lie offshore of Cape Hatteras and Ocracoke, respectively. According to the North Carolina Department of Environmental Quality (DEQ), the material now sits on the seafloor, adding new structure for marine life while improving opportunities for recreational fishing and diving. The concrete was donated by businesses and the North Carolina Department of Transportation, which had material that was damaged and no longer usable for its original purpose. The project was part of a year-long process involving public comment, planning, permitting and stockpiling before the material could be deployed.The concrete was added to two established reefsAR-230, also known as the Mr. J.C. Reef, is approximately 6 miles from Hatteras Inlet in about 70 feet of water. The site already contains several large structures, including the 105-foot tug Mr. J.C., which was sunk there in 1987, as well as a 75-foot landing craft and 130-foot freighter added in 1991. The latest project placed the new concrete material in a dense field around the existing reef.AR-250 lies approximately 10 miles from Ocracoke Inlet in about 80 feet of water. Its earlier materials include concrete rubble deployed between 1990 and 1992, a bridge frame added in 2001 and concrete boxes placed between 2005 and 2006. The new 1,500-ton addition further increases the amount of hard structure available at the site. The use of existing reef sites means the project was an enhancement rather than the creation of two entirely new artificial reefs. North Carolina's Artificial Reef Program has been creating and expanding reef sites since the 1970s, using materials including concrete, vessels and other suitable structures.Damaged concrete gets another use underwaterThe material used for the latest projects came from across North Carolina. DEQ said businesses and the N.C. Department of Transportation donated concrete pipe and boxes that had been damaged and were unusable for their intended purposes. Instead of being discarded, the material was transported, stockpiled and eventually deployed on the two offshore reefs.Once on the seafloor, concrete provides hard surfaces and three-dimensional structure in areas where naturally occurring rocky habitat is limited. The Artificial Reef Program says its reef materials are strategically located to maximise access for anglers and divers while also serving biological and ecological purposes. The programme describes the reefs as habitat for marine organisms as well as destinations for recreational users. The two sites are already popular with anglers. DEQ says fishermen visiting both reefs can expect to catch triggerfish, black sea bass and other bottom-dwelling fish, while divers often report underwater visibility of more than 50 feet.Fish can begin using new structures quicklyMarine life can colonise artificial reef structures surprisingly quickly, although the timing and species involved vary from site to site. In 2022, Artificial Reef Program coordinator Jordan Byrum recalled seeing fish around a tugboat near Pine Knoll Shores only 30 to 45 minutes after it was sunk. Byrum was on a dive at the time and said fish had already gathered around the vessel. That observation involved a different reef and was not a measurement of how quickly fish colonised the new material at AR-230 or AR-250. The broader objective of the programme is to build increasingly complex reef structures that can provide shelter and feeding areas for marine organisms while supporting recreational fishing and diving. North Carolina has repeatedly used donated and recycled materials for this purpose, including large quantities of concrete from transportation projects.North Carolina maintains dozens of artificial reefsThe latest additions are part of a much larger statewide programme. The Artificial Reef Program, operated by the N.C. Division of Marine Fisheries within the Department of Environmental Quality, currently maintains 43 ocean artificial reefs and 29 estuarine reefs. Reef locations and enhancement materials are selected based on factors including public input, available materials, existing structures and the potential to increase habitat complexity.The state has previously undertaken much larger reef projects. In 2022, for example, material from the old Oregon Inlet bridge was distributed among eight artificial reefs, with approximately 80,000 tons of concrete deployed in total. That project was described by DEQ as the largest amount of material associated with an artificial reef project in the programme's history. The 2026 work at AR-230 and AR-250 is considerably smaller, but it follows the same principle: material that can no longer serve its original purpose can instead become part of a permanent underwater structure. At the two Outer Banks sites, the latest 3,000 tons of recycled concrete now form additional reef habitat on the seafloor.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Two arrested over Grand Burstin hotel fire in Folkestone
articles.summary: A 38-year-old man and 21-year-old woman were arrested on suspicion of arson, police say.
articles.body:
Two people have been arrested on suspicion of arson after a fire at a seaside hotel which led to hundreds of people being evacuated.

Kent Police said a 38-year-old man and 21-year-old woman were held after the blaze at the Grand Burstin Hotel in Folkestone on Saturday.

The fire broke out at the hotel in Marine Parade in the early hours and about 280 people were evacuated from the building.

A total of 90 people were relocated from neighbouring Pavilion Court in Marine Terrace following concerns raised by safety inspectors, Folkestone and Hythe District Council said.

The pair who were arrested have been released while inquiries continue, a police spokesperson said.

Police say road closures remain in place for investigation work following the blaze, which started at about 01:20 BST.

The blaze is being treated as suspicious and police are appealing for witnesses.

Britannia Hotels Group, which runs the Grand Burstin, said at the weekend it was fully cooperating with police and supporting the investigation.

The group said engineers and building inspectors had been at the site to carry out structural assessments, and its team was working to assist guests.

Twenty six fire engines were sent to the hotel and Kent Fire and Rescue Service said it was believed the fire had started in the basement of the building.

Folkestone & Hythe District Council says it has been working to arrange alternative housing for affected residents, including all tenants from Pavilion Court, while the hotel undergoes assessments and any required works to make it safe.

On Saturday, a welfare centre was set up for hotel residents.

Other businesses, including nearby pub The Harbour Inn, also opened their doors to those affected.

Ross Honeycombe, who was staying at the hotel with his family, described how they were woken by fire alarms at about 01:00, adding: "We looked out and there was smoke billowing from the underground car park.

A resident at Pavilion Court, John Dighton, said he "grabbed stuff for a couple of days" and was staying at a nearby hotel.

He said the worst thing was not knowing how long they would be away from their homes.

articles.title: Two New York brothers started experimenting with CNC machining in their parents' garage; today, they run a high-tech company making parts for aerospace and medical industries
articles.summary: US News: Two brothers from New York transformed a pandemic-era experiment in their parents' garage into a precision manufacturing business serving technically .
articles.body: Two brothers from New York transformed a pandemic-era experiment in their parents' garage into a precision manufacturing business serving technically demanding industries. Sean and James Cerven began learning CNC machining in 2020 after purchasing a Tormach PCNC 440 milling machine. Working from their parents' garage in Poughkeepsie, they initially took on small jobs that helped them gain practical experience. As their interest in machining developed into a long-term business ambition, they established Cerven Solutions. The company later expanded beyond its garage workshop, joined the Xometry Partner Network and invested in advanced machinery and inspection equipment. Today, it produces complex, precision-machined components for the aerospace, defence, radar and satellite communications sectors.How two New York brothers turned a garage experiment into a high-tech companyDuring the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020, mechanical engineering students James and Sean Cerven began learning about CNC machining. The process uses computer-controlled machines to cut, drill and shape materials such as metal and plastic according to digital designs.After purchasing a Tormach PCNC 440 milling machine, the brothers began experimenting in their parents' garage in Poughkeepsie, New York. They initially received small jobs from customers, giving them an opportunity to build practical experience despite their limited background in commercial machining.As they became more familiar with designing and manufacturing components, the brothers realised they wanted to pursue machining professionally. They began developing their project into Cerven Solutions, turning their technical interests into a commercial manufacturing venture.While looking for additional customers, the brothers discovered Xometry through a machining group on Facebook. They contacted the company and subsequently purchased additional tooling and inspection equipment. After completing a test part, they joined the Xometry Partner Network, which connected them with potential manufacturing projects.The company soon outgrew its garage workshop as the volume of work increased. In its February 2025 case study, Xometry reported that Cerven Solutions had completed 671 projects through the platform and generated $1.5 million in Xometry revenue. The report also stated that the company had moved into a 3,000-square-foot workshop and was investing in additional machinery and quality-control equipment.Making precision components for specialised industriesCerven Solutions produces precision-machined components for aerospace, defence, satellite communications and other specialised technology sectors. The company lists capabilities including waveguides, split-block assemblies, RF couplers, power dividers, polarisers, radio-frequency housings, filter bodies and resonator cavities. It also lists antenna structures, optical and sensor housings, thermal-management components such as cold plates and heat spreaders, along with brackets and mounting hardware.For aerospace and unmanned aerial systems, the company lists structural fittings, hardpoints, motor and payload mounts, fins, canards and actuation fittings. Its listed capabilities also include power and battery enclosures, such as module housings, sealed lids and terminal plates. These examples come from Cerven Solutions' official website, which describes the types of hardware it builds rather than identifying specific customer orders.As Cerven Solutions expanded, the brothers invested in equipment designed to improve machining precision and production efficiency. The company's website lists a Matsuura MX-420 PC10 five-axis machining centre, FANUC RoboDrill machines and a Datron neo machining centre.It also lists a Zeiss DuraMax coordinate measuring machine for dimensional inspection. Such equipment allows manufacturers to check whether finished components meet the measurements and tolerances specified in engineering designs.Working with challenging materialsThe company works with materials including aluminium, titanium, stainless steel and high-performance plastics. Its website describes capabilities involving thin walls, deep pockets, tight corners and substantial material removal.These machining tasks require careful control because manufacturers must maintain dimensional accuracy while cutting away material. Cerven Solutions says it has developed processes to manage challenges such as chatter, wall taper and material stress when producing complex components. The company also states that it is working towards Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) Level 2 and is not currently certified under that standard.Sean and James Cerven began with a CNC milling machine in their parents' garage and initially relied on small customer jobs to build experience. As their confidence and ambitions grew, they developed the project into Cerven Solutions and explored ways to secure more manufacturing work.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Is it a missile? Is it a drone? What’s the Pelican used by Ukraine?
articles.summary: The use of the Pelican has provoked interest among military analysts as to whether it is a tactical ballistic missile.
articles.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Sunday’s large-scale strike on Russia involved several weapons, including a “Pelican” for the first time.

In a post on X on Sunday morning, Zelenskyy wrote that long-range attacks on Moscow’s region had a “very significant impact”.

“One of Russia’s key oil industry facilities and the aggressor’s logistics facility were hit. These are billions of dollars that sustain the war machine. The systems used included FP-1, RZ-100, MICH-2000, Palianytsia, Vendetta, Liutyi, Bars, Flamingo, Sichen and Pelican,” he said.

The attack on the final day of voting in Russia’s parliamentary elections killed at least three people. Moscow’s Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said more than 1,600 drones were intercepted, 450 of them heading for the capital.

However, the use of the Pelican has interested military analysts about whether it is a tactical ballistic missile or a drone.

What is a Pelican missile and why is there confusion?

Speaking at the 34th International Defence Industry Exhibition in Poland last week, the CEO of Ukrainian defence firm Fire Point said Ukraine could start deploying its FP-7 tactical ballistic missile to target Russia in weeks, reported The Kyiv Post.

Iryna Terekh explained that the new weapons could strike targets 200km (125 miles) away and carry a warhead weighing up to 150kg.

The FP-7 system is ground-launched and has a maximum projectile speed of 1,500 metres per second. Fire Point founder and chief designer Denys Shtilerman told Ukrainian media back in March that the system is cheaper than the US-made Army Tactical Missile Systems (ATACMS) surface-to-surface ballistic missiles.

Zelenskyy also said last month that they expected to use their first domestically produced ballistic missile as early as in the autumn.

So far, there is no official confirmation that the FP-7 tactical ballistic missile is the Pelican, but Ukrainian media, such as The Kyiv Post, has linked the two together.

The New Voice of Ukraine reported on Sunday that Fire Point, the Ukrainian company that also produces the FP-5 Flamingo cruise missile, had earlier this year applied to register the Pelican trademark.

However, the RBC-Ukraine news agency, citing unnamed sources, reported on Sunday without elaborating that the Pelican was an aircraft-type drone.

Al Jazeera could not independently verify the Ukrainian media reports.

What is Ukraine’s weapons production like?

In February, Ukraine’s defence ministry said that the domestic weapons industry had demonstrated “unprecedented growth”, with production capacity increasing 50-fold to $50bn.

“As a result, domestic manufacturers now meet over half of the Defence Forces’ needs for weapons and military equipment,” the ministry said.

On Saturday, Zelenskyy posted on X that the military counterintelligence unit at the Security Service of Ukraine has developed a new interceptor drone that had been “successfully deployed” against Iranian-made Shahed drones used by Russia throughout the war to target Ukraine.

“Step by step, we are moving forward to give Ukraine greater protection. I thank all the developers and manufacturers who work every day to scale up the weapons we need,” he said.

In March, Oleksandr Syrskyi, the former Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of Ukraine, said more than 70 per cent of Shahed-type attack drones were destroyed using interceptor drones in February.

The success of Ukraine’s drone interceptors also led to interest from Gulf states targeted by Iranian drones and missiles during the US-Israeli war.

How have attacks on Russia changed recently?

Both Russia and Ukraine have intensified attacks on each other’s infrastructure, targeting oil facilities and logistics hubs.

Ukraine has also repeatedly struck warehouses belonging to Russia’s Wildberries e-commerce giant since July, in what has been described as an attack on Moscow’s supply chains and to hurt the Russian economy.

On Monday, the Financial Times reported that US President Donald Trump spoke to Zelenskyy on Sunday, urging him to stop attacking Russian refineries over concerns that it was worsening the global shortage of diesel and causing fuel prices to increase.

articles.title: In 2008, a collector spotted an unusual Eisenhower dollar inside a tube of ordinary coins; one of only three known prototypes, it later sold for $264,000 and is now returning to auction
articles.summary: US News: An experimental 1971 Eisenhower dollar that spent decades hidden inside a tube of ordinary coins before selling for $264,000 (£199,000) has returned t.
articles.body: An experimental 1971 Eisenhower dollar that spent decades hidden inside a tube of ordinary coins before selling for $264,000 (£199,000) has returned to the auction block. The coin is one of only three known surviving prototypes of the United States Mint’s first space-themed dollar, according to a report published by CoinWeek. Catalogued as Judd-2147, the coin is scheduled to be sold by online auction house GreatCollections, with bidding set to close on October 18, 2026. Graded SP67 by the Professional Coin Grading Service (PCGS) and carrying a green Certified Acceptance Corporation (CAC) sticker, the coin is considered one of the most remarkable modern discoveries in American numismatics.Spotted inside a coin tubeThe discovery took place on February 15, 2008, at the Long Beach Coin Expo in California. Collector Lee C. Lydston was attending the show with his wife, Denise, when she noticed a dealer selling tubes containing 40 per cent silver Eisenhower dollars. While examining one of the tubes, Lydston pulled out a 1971-S dollar that looked very different from normal uncirculated coins and standard proof issues. Its surface had an unusual texture, the strike was extremely sharp, and the details of the Moon on the reverse did not match regular production coins. Realising that the coin did not fit known examples, Lydston bought it and sent it to specialists at the Ike Group for scientific testing.Clues on the MoonResearchers compared the coin with archival material and discovered that its reverse matched an early 1970 galvano held at the Dwight D. Eisenhower Presidential Library and Museum in Abilene, Kansas. The biggest difference can be seen on the Moon on the reverse. Chief Engraver Frank Gasparro had added detailed craters to the lunar surface during the early design process. However, many of those details were changed or removed before regular production began. The coin also shows heavy die-polishing lines, rough edges around some of the lettering, slight doubling of some design elements and an unusually strong strike. Later metallurgical testing by PCGS confirmed that the coin contains the standard 40 per cent silver and 60 per cent copper mix used for collector coins of the period.Press demonstrations and a minting challengeThe United States Mint faced major technical challenges while preparing the Eisenhower dollar for release in 1971. The coin marked the return of the dollar denomination after a 36-year break following the Peace dollar series in 1935. Gasparro's design showed General Eisenhower on the front and an adapted Apollo 11 mission patch on the back. The reverse featured an eagle carrying an olive branch above the Moon. Because the coin measured 38.5 millimetres across, Mint workers had difficulty producing the high-relief details without damaging the dies or minting equipment. According to historical records cited by CoinWeek, Mint Director Mary T. Brooks invited journalists to the Philadelphia Mint on January 25, 1971, to watch experimental trial strikes. Official documents said technicians prepared several prototype dies and 40 per cent silver blanks to test die shapes, planchet preparation and striking pressure. Mint rules required all trial coins made during the Philadelphia demonstration to be destroyed by the Director’s Trial Strike Committee.The mystery of the San Francisco markDespite those orders, three prototype dollars survived. All three known coins carry the "S" mintmark for the San Francisco Mint. Because of this, researchers at Heritage Auctions have suggested that the Mint may have sent prototype dies to San Francisco to test equipment intended for producing 40 per cent silver collector coins. However, it is still unknown exactly how the experimental coins left official Mint control and ended up in the public market, packaged inside standard Mint pliofilm wrappers known to collectors as "Blue Packs." For 37 years, the Lydston prototype remained completely unnoticed.Two more chance discoveriesTwo more examples were found in later years, confirming that the prototype series used two different die pairings. In 2010, collector Charles Chatham bought a second prototype inside an original Blue Pack at an Alabama pawn shop for just $10. It had the same prototype reverse die as Lydston's coin but used a different obverse die. The difference could be seen in variations in the lettering of the word "LIBERTY." A third prototype was found on eBay in 2013 by an alert collector. That coin used the exact same die pairing as Lydston's discovery and was later graded PCGS SP66.A quarter-million-dollar milestoneThe extreme rarity of the three prototypes is striking when compared with the number of regular coins produced. The San Francisco Mint struck more than 6.8 million uncirculated silver dollars and more than 4 million silver proof dollars in 1971 alone. Lydston's discovery was later acquired by collector David Frohman. In January 2022, Heritage Auctions sold the PCGS SP67 example for $264,000, setting an auction record for the Judd-2147 designation. The coin now being offered by GreatCollections, under certification number 55926571, remains the only one of the three known prototypes to receive CAC approval. It is also the highest-graded example known.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Gang stole £600k of Land Rover Defenders for 'chop shop'
articles.summary: The men from Worcestershire and Bristol took 33 Land Rovers in eight months.
articles.body:
A gang who stole 33 Land Rover Defenders worth more than £600,000 in just eight months have been jailed.

The four men targeted vehicles across six police force areas between September 2024 and May 2025, including in Worcestershire, Herefordshire, Gloucestershire and Powys.

All four pleaded guilty to conspiracy to steal vehicles and were sentenced at Hereford Crown Court on Friday.

West Mercia Police said the Defenders were stolen from locations including Malvern, Bromyard, Droitwich, Leominster, Tenbury Wells, Suckley, Kingsland and Storridge.

Other thefts took place in Gloucestershire, Bath, Powys, Sussex, Devon and Cornwall.

West Mercia Police launched Operation Liondale following Butler's arrest in November 2025.

Officers said distinctive clothing, seen on CCTV as the offences were committed, was found in Butler's caravan.

Police officer relives race to save trapped driver

Leonard Hodgkins, 50, of Marlborough Gardens, Malvern, was jailed for four years and nine months.

Jimmy Butler, 42, of Waterside Park, Offerton Lane, Worcester, was sentenced to four years, one month and six days, while Benjamin Hobbs, 36, of Beesmoor Road, Bristol, was jailed for four years and eight months.

David Hodgkins, 41, of The Furlong, Powick, was sentenced to three years.

His co-conspirators were arrested on 11 November 2025, with police saying mobile phone evidence showed the gang travelled in convoy with the stolen vehicles.

Hobbs owned a workshop in Bristol which police said was being used as a "chop shop", where stolen vehicles were dismantled for parts.

Parts from the stolen Land Rovers were discovered there, with some identified by their owners and others confirmed using keys concealed in the vehicles.

Police said automatic number plate recognition cameras and phone evidence also linked members of the gang to the stolen vehicles.

Detective Sergeant Mark Jones, of Hereford CID, said: "We know it often seems like car thieves get away with it, but we hope this result shows we will always work hard to bring these offenders before the courts and try to halt the impact their actions have on our communities."

articles.title: Edinburgh Airport to expand terminal in £500m investment plan
articles.summary: The project includes new gates and aircraft stands, an expanded check-in hall and departure lounge, with new food and retail areas.
articles.body:
Edinburgh Airport has unveiled a £500m investment programme to expand its terminal and improve facilities over the next five years.

The project includes new gates and aircraft stands, an expanded check-in hall and departure lounge, new food and retail areas and a 60% larger terminal footprint.

Airport bosses said it would support new long and short haul routes, and grow international connectivity at Scotland's busiest terminal.

The investment also includes improvements across the airport campus, with additional electric vehicle infrastructure and a new access road.

More stories from Edinburgh, Fife & East

First Minister John Swinney visited the airport's South East Pier expansion, the first phase of the development due to open in summer 2027.

Swinney said: "This significant investment will enable Edinburgh Airport to compete with airports around the world.

"Alongside delivering real benefits to passengers, this boost will support Scotland's international connections and help drive economic growth.

"Scotland is open for business and we want to maintain and strengthen Scotland's position as the most attractive place in the UK for inward investment outside of London and the South East."

Edinburgh Airport is Scotland's busiest airport and served about 17 million passengers in 2025.

It has 39 airlines and flying to more than 160 destinations, including major hubs in the UK, Europe, USA, and the Middle and Far East

Chief executive Gordon Dewar said: "This is the biggest investment in Edinburgh Airport's history and comes at one of the most exciting points in its development, adding another important chapter to its story.

"This is the first phase of a multi-year plan that ensures we are building for our future, creating the capacity, capability and customer experience we need and want."

The airport is jointly-owned by Vinci Airports, which has a 50.01% stake, and Global Infrastructure Partners managing the remaining 49.99%

Vinci is the world's biggest private airport operator, with more than 70 airports in 14 countries.

Global Infrastructure Partners (GIP), part of BlackRock, is an investor that specialises in energy, transport and digital infrastructure.

The £500m announcement came on the same day as a "technical issue" with air traffic control in Scotland brought flight delays at Edinburgh and several other UK airports.

The air traffic service control service Nats said engineers had fixed the problem at its Prestwick centre, which handles air traffic control across Scotland and the north of England.

Nats said the issue was not related to a software defect that led to the cancellation of 2,000 flights across the UK earlier this month.

articles.summary: Middle East News: Despite Yemen's plea for US military support, president Donald Trump stopped short of committing American forces to counter the Houthis during a call .
articles.body: Despite Yemen's plea for US military support, president Donald Trump stopped short of committing American forces to counter the Houthis during a call with Yemeni president Rashad al-Alimi on Sunday.Alimi had sought Washington’s backing for his Saudi-backed government after the Iran-aligned Houthis rapidly seized key areas along Yemen’s Red Sea coast, particularly around the strategically vital Bab al-Mandeb Strait.According to sources cited by Reuters, Trump made no direct pledge of military assistance during the call.Earlier, US officials had reportedly met Houthi representatives at the US embassy in Muscat, organised by the longtime regional mediator, Oman. The Houthis had affirmed their commitment to the 2025 ceasefire, saying no commercial ships would be targeted in the Bab-el-Mandeb strait, except the Saudis. Reuters reported.Nearly seven-month-old Iran conflict has already kept US forces in deep waters, with the Mandeb strait acting as an alternative to Hormuz. In such a case, a US military campaign in the now Houthi dominated waters could prove disastrous for the regional allies and overall global trade.U-turn at the last momentAccording to The New York Times, Trump administration had prepared to launch airstrikes against the Houthis on Sunday, following fresh pleas from the Saudi crown prince. However, the newspaper reported that Trump called off the strikes at the last minute.Two people briefed on the operation said Trump pulled back from, or at least delayed, striking Houthi targets even as commanders had approved target lists and troops were loading bombs onto US warplanes chosen for the missions, with the wave of attacks about to begin.Trump had reportedly met with advisers the previous day and told them he was not in favour of the strikes.The Houthis have fought against the Saudi-led coalition for more than a decade. Tensions reignited in July when the group declared a blockade on Saudi shipping in the Red Sea as a response to the Saudi blockade of Yemen's ports.According to Reuters, Saudi forces have launched hundreds of strikes in recent days on Houthi positions in the highlands.The United Nations has reported that nearly 700 people have been killed and thousands injured in the flare-up in fighting, with nearly 130,000 Yemenis displaced within the country and more than 3,000 fleeing by boat across the Red Sea to Africa.On Sunday, Trump said he remained in “deciding mode” over the Middle East situation, this includes whether to protect its long term regional ally, or maintain truce with the Iran-backed group.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: A 1762 Virginia house stood in Sussex County for 184 years, then was dismantled piece by piece in 1946 and rebuilt on land once part of George Washington's Mount Vernon estate; listing now contingent at $3.799 million
articles.summary: Real Estate News: A historic 1762 Virginia farmhouse that spent its first 184 years in Sussex County before being taken apart and moved timber by timber has a prospecti.
articles.body: A historic 1762 Virginia farmhouse that spent its first 184 years in Sussex County before being taken apart and moved timber by timber has a prospective buyer at $3.799 million (£2.86 million). According to property records and estate reports from Realtor.com, the five-bedroom home is located at 4509 Carlby Lane in Alexandria, along the Potomac River. The land was once part of George Washington’s Mount Vernon estate. The property is currently listed as contingent after being marketed by estate agents Andrea Courduvelis and Diane G. Murphy of TTR Sotheby’s International Realty. Known as Carlby, the 2,992-square-foot home is a rare example of historic preservation and has remained with the same family for three generations.Moved piece by pieceThe house was originally built in 1762 in Sussex County, Virginia, where it was known as the Mitchell House. It stayed in its original rural location until 1946, when Carl W. Porter, a retired United States Navy captain and former Fairfax County director of public works, bought the property. Wanting to protect the historic structure, Porter led a major relocation project. Workers carefully took the house apart timber by timber and labelled each piece before transporting the materials north to a 2.18-acre waterfront property in Alexandria. Co-listing agent Andrea Courduvelis told Realtor.com about the detailed work carried out by the family patriarch. "Carl Porter bought the house where it was in Sussex County, took it apart piece by piece, labeled each piece and put it back together on the property it sits on today," Courduvelis said. "The property has stayed within the family for three generations." Porter and his wife, Beatrice, named the rebuilt home Carlby after completing the project.Historical links and original featuresThe home has important historical connections beyond its link to land associated with George Washington. A 1976 study by historian Barbara Spann for the Fairfax County History Commission identified Carlby as the boyhood home of General Winfield Scott. Scott was a major military figure who served in the War of 1812, the Mexican-American War and the American Civil War. Inside, the house still has many of its original 18th-century features. These include wide-plank pine floors, 12-foot ceilings, floor-to-ceiling windows, original wood paneling painted in traditional period colors and several working fireplaces. The dining room has a custom chandelier designed by Porter himself. It was based on an original light fixture at Gunston Hall, the historic home of Virginia founding father George Mason.Courduvelis said the design of the house also reflects the way people lived during the colonial period. "What is now considered the rear entrance was originally the home's primary entrance, as visitors commonly arrived by water or horseback," Courduvelis told Realtor.com. "From today's front door, you can see straight through the house to the Potomac River. This is a design that was characteristic of the time period, but is unique today." The only major interior change came in the 1990s, when the second generation of the Porter family renovated the kitchen. According to the listing agents, the kitchen is still the only part of the main house that differs significantly from the original 1762 design.Waterfront grounds and private featuresThe 2.18-acre property has 151 feet of direct frontage on the Potomac River, along with a private pier. Other structures on the grounds include a historic smokehouse, an outbuilding shed and a detached two-car garage. Courduvelis said the property's privacy and setting have been major attractions for potential buyers during viewings. "Many have commented on how it feels like you are stepping back in time the moment you turn into the private driveway," Courduvelis told Realtor.com. "The expansive waterfront views are extraordinary and create an incredible sense of peace and tranquility." She also said the combination of original 18th-century materials and the riverfront location makes the property very different from modern homes in Fairfax County. "Together, these elements give Carlby a warmth, authenticity, and sense of history that simply cannot be re-created in a newly built home," Courduvelis said. articles.title: Indian-yoga teachers row sparks debate, as Australia tightens immigration rules
articles.summary: Rest of World News: Australia's immigration debate has turned the spotlight on international students, temporary visa pathways and a claim involving yoga teachers, with T.
articles.body: Australia's immigration debate has turned the spotlight on international students, temporary visa pathways and a claim involving yoga teachers, with Tony Burke, immigration minister, seeking to draw a distinction between legitimate migration and the vias-hopping.In his recent address to the National Press Club, Burke said the government supported immigration as a contributor to Australia's economy but wanted greater control over a system that had historically relied heavily on demand-driven migration.Addressing claims that Australia was bringing in more yoga teachers than construction workers, Burke said: “There is an endless refrain that the government is bringing in yoga teachers and not construction workers, to the extent that the shadow minister for housing, Senator Bragg, has even said we are bringing in more yoga teachers than construction workers.”Debunking this claim, he pointed out that the number of construction workers brought in during the previous financial year was just under 15,000, compared with 4,500 earlier. “We've tripled the number of construction workers who are coming in,” he said and added that the number of yoga teachers brought in under the current government was zero.Burke said yoga teachers appeared on the relevant occupation list because of an agreement made by a previous government with India. The minister attributed the agreement's announcement to Dan Tehan, who was then an assistant trade minister.TOI reviewed the relevant trade agreement. The Australia–India Economic Cooperation and Trade Agreement, signed in April 2022 which entered into force in Dec 2022, contains a provision allowing for the temporary entry of up to 1,800 qualified professional Indian traditional chefs and yoga instructors annually under the ‘contractual service supplier category’.Burke also holds various other portfolios including Home Affairs. His comments come as Australia seeks to manage the economic and infrastructure implications of migration while maintaining the benefits of international education.Visa hopping under scrutinyBurke also addressed concerns around international students moving from one visa category to another. He stressed that not all visa transitions should be considered visa hopping.He described a legitimate pathway in which a student completes a qualification in an area of skill shortage, moves to a graduate visa, finds relevant employment, obtains employer sponsorship and potentially progresses to permanent residency and citizenship.However, the minister said the government was concerned about cases where people who would not meet the requirements for permanent residency repeatedly moved between visas and used appeal processes to be able to stay here as long as possible. “It eventually becomes absurd to not just let them stay, because at that point they have Australian citizen children and at that point they are so integrated into a local community,” he stated.To curb visa hopping - students repeatedly moving between courses and institutions primarily to pursue a migration outcome rather than an educational qualification, he said that while course extensions and legitimate transfers will remain permitted, students will generally be expected to progress up the qualification ladder, such as moving from a bachelor's degree to a master's, rather than repeatedly shifting between courses at different levels.Indian students accounted for 16% of Australia's international student population in the first five months of 2026, making India the country's second-largest source market after China (23%), according to Australian government data. The figures translate to approximately a little over one lakh Indian students during the period as opposed to nearly 1.6 lakh Chinese students. Thus, policy changes would impact the Indian diaspora and aspiring students.Further, Australia will no longer generally allow international students and graduate visa holders to automatically bring family members to the country under proposed migration changes. He clarified that existing families already in Australia will not be separated under the new rules, and exemptions will apply to students from Pacific and ASEAN nations (India does not fall in these categories) and those enrolled in certain courses, including PhD programmes.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Cairngorms crofters and farmers call for new wildfire action plan
articles.summary: A meeting was held on the back of this summer's wildfire, which burned for almost five weeks.
articles.body:
Crofters and farmers in the Cairngorms are calling for a new, comprehensive plan to deal with moorland fires to be put in place within six months.

The demand follows a second major summer wildfire in as many years in the UK's largest national park.

The plea was made to Agriculture Minister Jim Fairlie and a senior officer from the Scottish Fire and Rescue Service (SFRS) during a public meeting in Aveimore on Friday.

More than 300 people attended the gathering, organised by the group Cairngorms Crofters and Farmers.

It came after Highland Council agreed to write to the Scottish government seeking an independent review of the incident.

The Scottish government previously said a multi-agency review and debrief would be carried out into the wildfire.

More stories from the Highlands and Islands

News from the Highlands and Islands on BBC Sounds

Firefighters, gamekeepers and land managers spent almost five weeks tackling the wildfire which broke out in the Glenmore area on 15 July.

The fire destroyed about 10 sq miles (25 sq km) of moorland and forestry, with the damage described as 'apocalyptic' .

A major incident was declared on day 10, with some residents and businesses evacuated from Nethy Bridge.

Robert MacDonald, chairman of Cairngorms Crofters and Farmers, said they had received assurances at Friday's meeting.

"We were assured that they were making all the efforts possible to put protocols in place and that they hoped to have systems going forward that would enable them to bring fires like this under control a lot quicker and a lot more efficiently," he said.

Agriculture Minister Jim Fairlie said he valued the opportunity to meet with community groups.

He added: "It was important that I heard directly from those affected, to understand their experiences and ensure their voices shape future response and recovery efforts.

"The strength and resilience shown by local communities during this difficult time was articulated loud and clear during the meeting."

Fairlie pledged the review would identify issues arising from the wildfire.

He said: "We recognise the importance of land management practices that help mitigate against the risk and spread of wildfire, including through regulated muirburn, the creation of fire breaks and other methods of vegetation management.

"Going forward, better communication with community groups and land managers will be essential in tackling wildfires effectively."

SFRS deputy assistant chief officer Kenny Barbour said it was important to record the views of the community.

"I would like to thank everyone who attended the meeting to share their insights, which will be captured in the formal debrief to ensure learnings are identified," he said.

"We will of course reflect on the findings to ensure we continue to enhance our operational response in the future."

He confirmed the fire service was developing a new long term wildfire strategy.

And he added: "We are committed to enhancing partnership working to meet future challenges and build resilience in our communities."

Last month, Scotland's chief fire officer called for an improved, more formal approach to wildfire prevention in order to "protect lives".

Meanwhile more than £500,000 has been distributed to support businesses affected by the Cairngorms wildfire.

The Scottish government's Cairngorms Fire Recovery Fund is being administered by Highland Council and 14 grants have so far been paid to businesses.

articles.title: Cleveland Police in post-A66 crash organised crime raids
articles.summary: The raids across Teesside follow the A66 crash which killed two police officers and five men.
articles.body:
Police have carried out a series of early morning raids targeting those suspected of being involved in organised crime.

Cleveland Police said 17 people had been arrested during the operation - involving about 130 officers including some from the National Crime Agency - across South Bank, Grangetown and Eston, near Middlesbrough, on Monday.

It is part of a high-profile response to a crash on the nearby A66 last month which came at the end of a police pursuit and left two officers dead.

Five men died also died when their Volkswagen Passat went the wrong way down the road and hit a Cleveland Police armed response vehicle heading in the opposite direction.

The force said Monday's raids had seen people arrested on suspicion of various offences including drugs and assault.

A convoy of about a dozen vans started the operation shortly after 08:00 BST, with roads temporarily blocked by patrol cars.

Officers used battering rams to force entry to several properties as parents walked past with their children on the school run.

Assistant Chief Constable Mark Hall said public support after the crash had been ''absolutely phenomenal".

"It's clear criminality of any sort is not welcome on these estates and we are here to tell those people we've heard their concerns and we will act," he said.

Officers PC Matthew Blades, 37, and PC Tom Clough, 38, along with all five occupants of the Passat died at the scene of the A66 crash.

Cleveland's Police and Crime Commissioner Matt Storey said it was important for people to see officers on the streets targeting those responsible for crime.

He said: "This makes people more reassured about what is really going in their communities. They see people arrested, charged and taken off the streets.

"It shows the public good work is happening, despite the problems we have."

articles.title: I've got no ceiling on Lib Dem ambitions, says leader Ed Davey
articles.summary: The Lib Dem leader also backed the controversial Jackdaw gas field, which the government is expected to approve.
articles.body:
Lib Dem leader Sir Ed Davey has insisted he is not just aiming to be a junior partner in a coalition government, saying: "I am a candidate to be prime minister."

He also backed the controversial Jackdaw gas field, which the government is expected to green light later this month, saying it had "passed the climate test" and was compatible with a transition to renewables.

Sir Ed has faced criticism from some in his party that he lacks ambition and the vision needed to cut through in a crowded political field.

He acknowledged the "frustration" felt by some of his MPs that the party was not making a bigger impact - and vowed to set out bold policies in his conference speech on Tuesday.

Sir Ed led the Lib Dems to a record 72 MPs at the 2024 election, making big gains at the expense of the Conservatives in southern England, but the party has since slipped to fourth or fifth in national opinion polls, behind Labour, the Tories, the Greens and Reform UK.

Despite this, the Lib Dem leader claimed his party had an "historic opportunity to do far better than anyone imagines at the moment" at the next general election.

"Because the right wing is split," he said, "and fragmented like it's never happened before in over 200 years of British parliamentary elections.

"If we take that opportunity, and I believe we're showing how we can, we'll be a massive force in the next parliament."

Asked if he wanted to be the kingmaker in the next government, providing support for a party falling short of the 326 MPs needed for a majority, Sir Ed said: "I've got no ceiling on our ambitions.

"I'm a candidate to be prime minister, but what we need to do is make sure that we build on that [election success], area by area, constituency by constituency."

He made clear he will not go into a coalition government with Reform UK and has dismissed suggestions he could do a deal with the Conservatives.

"We've got a moral responsibility to stop Nigel Farage - and indeed stop Kemi Badenoch giving the keys to No 10 to Nigel Farage - I think there could be that sort of coalition on the right and we've got to stop that," he told the BBC.

Asked if he would form a coalition with Labour, he said he did not deal in "hypotheticals".

He said he wanted the Lib Dems to win support across the UK, but the BBC has been told his party's strategy is focused on the 27 seats where they came second in 2024. Of those 27, 20 are held by the Conservatives.

Controversial Jackdaw gas field set to be approved in weeks, sources say

Sir Ed was speaking just before he headed out to visit the wind farm off the coast of Brighton, which he said he had signed off on when he was energy secretary in the Conservative-Lib Dem coalition government a decade ago.

He set out why supporting Jackdaw was not in conflict with his party's stance on tackling climate change, saying: "We're going to need gas for a long, long time as part of our transition, and when I was secretary of state for climate change, I always thought that we were going to need gas, and [Jackdaw] has passed the climate change test."

Sir Ed explained the alternative was shipping in liquified natural gas (LNG) from across the globe, which would be more problematic than using gas from the North Sea, about 150 miles northeast of Aberdeen.

"There's a lot of energy produced in both putting the gas into liquid and then taking it out into gas," he said.

"The carbon footprint of that is far bigger, a lot more damaging for our climate, so this way, not only is it better for the climate, but also tax revenues come to the Exchequer."

However, he told the BBC "the jury is very much out" on the Rosebank oil field, not least because that may not pass the same test on reducing carbon emissions.

And he insisted the Lib Dems were still committed to a transition away from oil and gas, for the climate and also to lower people's energy bills.

"Thanks to President Trump's mad war in Iran, people are paying far higher," he said. "We are paying far higher for that fossil fuel energy, and you've seen over the years how fossil fuels, oil and gas, can be extremely expensive.

"So, the way to get energy bills down, get the economy growing, is to be less dependent on fossil fuels and we want to be."

articles.title: Suspects in Haitian president's assassination transferred to Miami, accused of funding plot with COVID fraud
articles.summary: Exclusive video shows 18 shackled suspects arriving in Miami after transfer in the assassination of Haitian President Jovenel Moïse case.
articles.body: Eighteen allegedly involved in the brazen 2021 assassination of Haitian President Jovenel Moïse have touched down on U.S. soil to face federal charges, with Fox News cameras on the tarmac for their arrival Sunday. In exclusive footage, the defendants can be seen stepping off a U.S. military aircraft in Miami, shackled and tightly guarded by FBI and Department of Homeland Security agents in military-like fatigues. The dramatic transfer marks a major turning point in the international investigation into the plot that left the Haitian leader dead in his bedroom. "Today, the FBI and our interagency partners executed the largest foreign transfer of custody in FBI history," FBI Director Kash Patel told Fox News Digital in a statement. "It is the latest in an all-out 18-month blitz by this FBI man-hunting high-value targets across the world and bringing them back to the United States to face justice." FBI EXTRADITES FORMER TEN MOST WANTED FUGITIVE ARRESTED FOR 2000 MURDER OF 5-YEAR-OLD GIRL IN PHILADELPHIA The ​53-year-old president was shot dead in July 2021 at his private residence in ​the hills above Port-au-Prince, a killing that left a gaping political vacuum ⁠in the Caribbean nation and emboldened powerful armed groups in the country. According to FBI Miami, the accused — comprising operatives from Haiti and Colombia — were transferred from Haitian custody to face the U.S. justice system. Federal prosecutors established jurisdiction because the conspiracy was largely organized and financed in South Florida. Prosecutors allege the defendants utilized fraudulent COVID-19 Paycheck Protection Program (PPP) loans to bankroll the deadly mission. A complex five-year federal investigation into 30 suspects charged with crimes revealed the assassination was financed by American taxpayer dollars to businesses based in Florida to gather the weapons, tactical gear, and Colombian mercenaries that killed Moise inside his own home. The charges include conspiracy to kill or kidnap a person abroad, as well as wire fraud. Some of the assassins even allegedly posed as federal agents with the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) in order to get inside the presidential residence in Haiti. MAN PLEADS GUILTY TO STEALING OVER $1M IN PPP LOANS FOR SUPPOSED AMATEUR BASKETBALL LEAGUE As the 18 suspects arrived in Miami, Department of Justice prosecutors unsealed an indictment detailing the sprawling conspiracy. Court documents outline a plot initially aimed at violently overthrowing the Haitian President, which ultimately escalated into an assassination. This was "really about greed," Miami Special Agent in Charge Brett Skiles told Fox News. "These were people that owned business interests in the United States that were looking to get lucrative contracts from the government of Haiti and believed that if they could initiate a regime change to the assassination, that those contracts could then come their way, and they would profit off of it." The defendants were making their first appearance in federal court in Miami Monday morning. Because cameras are strictly prohibited inside federal courtrooms, the exclusive tarmac video serves as the only visual of the suspects entering U.S. custody. "This assassination plot was planned, financed, conspired, here in Miami," U.S. Attorney for the Southern District of Florida Jason Reding Quiñones told Fox News. "It's not only just holding people accountable for committing murder, but it's holding people accountable if they use government funds in a fraud to facilitate that murder." KASH PATEL REVEALS FBI'S CAPTURE OF ALL 10 MEMBERS OF MOST WANTED FUGITIVE'S LIST DURING HEARING The four ringleaders of this 2021 assassination plot were convicted in Miami in May and they face life in prison. Prosecutors ⁠argued during the nine-week trial in a Miami federal court that the men assembled two dozen former Colombian soldiers and supplied them ​with money, guns, ammunition and tactical vests. "When you pick up the phone and engage with foreign partners at a historic level, as we’ve done – a 400% increase these last 18 months – this is what happens," Patel's statement concluded. "Thank you to FBI Miami for their leadership in this investigation as well as our law enforcement partners who executed." Haitian Justice Minister Patrick ​Pelissier confirmed in a statement that suspects had been transferred from Haiti to the US, adding that Haitian judicial proceedings had been delayed. "While the American procedure has recorded significant progress, notably arrests, prosecutions, and ​convictions, the Haitian procedure remains confronted with major difficulties and has not, to date, resulted ​in a trial being held, after five years of proceedings," Pelissier said. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP In ⁠Haiti, prominent human rights activist Pierre Espérance said that the slow pace of the Haitian case and the transfer of the 18 suspects to the U.S. was a "disgrace for the Haitian ⁠justice system." He ​argued for strengthening the country's justice system to allow ​for such complex cases to be tried inside Haiti, rather than sending them to the U.S. for prosecution. Reuters contributed to this report.

articles.title: In 1968, California miner Joe Cullen found a 14.5-ounce gold nugget; 58 years later, the historic “Cullen Nugget” sold for $71,875
articles.summary: US News: California miner Joe Cullen found a substantial gold nugget at the Ruby Mine in Sierra County in 1968. Nearly six decades later, the 14.51-troy-ounce .
articles.body: California miner Joe Cullen found a substantial gold nugget at the Ruby Mine in Sierra County in 1968. Nearly six decades later, the 14.51-troy-ounce specimen known as the “Cullen Nugget” sold for $71,875 at Heritage Auctions' Nature and Science Signature Auction on April 29, 2026. The nugget weighs 451.41 grams and measures 2.44 by 2.24 by 0.77 inches. Heritage identifies it as native gold from the Ruby Mine on Mineral Mountain, part of the historic Alleghany Mining District, also known as the Forest Mining District. Its documented ownership history stretches from Cullen to W. Leicht, then to the J. Marshall Collection in 1993, before the specimen entered a private collection in the northeastern United States. Nearly 60 years after it was pulled from the California mine, the nugget returned to the auction market with its discovery and ownership history intact.Joe Cullen's 1968 discovery became a documented collector's specimenThe nugget's name comes directly from its original finder. Heritage describes the piece as the “Cullen Nugget”, named in honour of Joe Cullen, who collected it in 1968. Labels on the back of the specimen identify its association with the Ruby Mine in Sierra County. Its provenance then records the W. Leicht Collection, followed by the J. Marshall Collection, where it was catalogued in 1993 as #JHM4155, and finally a private Northeast Collection. That chain is significant for a mineral specimen because it connects the object being sold in 2026 with a specific discovery nearly 60 years earlier. Heritage describes the nugget as having a rounded, broad-disc form, a rich golden colour and a network of shallow cavities containing reddish-orange matrix. The auction house also notes its strong surface lustre and the natural shaping visible across the specimen. At 451.41 grams, the specimen weighs 14.51 troy ounces. Its relatively large surface area also gives the nugget a strong visual presence beyond its weight alone.The Ruby Mine sits in a historic California gold districtThe Ruby Mine lies in the Alleghany Mining District of Sierra County, a region with a long history of gold mining. Heritage describes the locality as a prolific gold-producing area that has been active since the 1850s, during the California Gold Rush. The district is also associated with the Forest Mining District name. The area became known for both lode and placer mining. Historical accounts of the Alleghany District identify the Ruby, Live Yankee and Bald Mountain drift mines among the major producers of the buried Tertiary gold channels. The Ruby Mine in particular produced coarse gold nuggets, with historical records noting that fist-sized nuggets were recovered there during the 1930s. The district is also home to the famous Sixteen-to-One Mine at Alleghany. The mine was incorporated in 1911 and became one of the best-known high-grade gold operations in the region. Records from the mine state that more than 1.1 million troy ounces of gold had been recovered from the Sixteen-to-One operation by 2011.The specimen's appearance reflects its natural historyUnlike a refined gold bar, a natural nugget retains the physical features created during its formation and subsequent movement through its environment. Heritage describes the Cullen Nugget as having a broad, rounded shape rather than a sharply defined crystalline form, with shallow cavities and areas of reddish-orange matrix across its surface. The auction house says those textures reflect both the nugget's primary formation and its later natural shaping. Its relatively large surface area also gives the specimen a strong visual presence beyond its weight alone. The dimensions help illustrate its unusual proportions. The nugget measures just over 6.2 centimetres long, 5.7 centimetres wide and 2 centimetres thick. At 451.41 grams, it is substantially heavier than an ordinary piece of jewellery-grade gold while retaining the irregular form of naturally occurring gold.The Cullen Nugget sold nearly 60 years after its discoveryHeritage offered the specimen as Lot 72086 in its April 29, 2026 Nature and Science Signature Auction. The auction record lists the final sale price at $71,875, with the winning bid coming from an internet bidder. The price places the Cullen Nugget among the notable gold specimens sold during that auction. Other gold pieces in the same sale included a 55.16-troy-ounce Australian nugget that sold for $262,500 and an 11.10-troy-ounce crystallised gold nugget from an unspecified locality that sold for $50,000. For the Cullen Nugget, however, its value as a collector's specimen rests on more than its weight. The piece carries a documented connection to a named miner, a specific California mine and a sequence of collections stretching back to its 1968 discovery. After changing hands several times, the nugget's latest sale has added another chapter to the documented history of a piece of natural gold from one of California's historic mining districts.Catch the latest World News and Live updates.
